title: Border and Ghost
premise: Ivo Voss, a whistle-blower living under four names, is hired to trace a passenger jet that vanished from every radar, database, and memory mid-flight—yet 212 people boarded it and their families remember. As he digs, he finds the erasure was engineered by a tri-government program preparing a summit treaty built on the disappeared flight's secret cargo. Hunted by an assassin who once saved his life, Ivo must smuggle the recovered black box truth past three governments before the summit convenes, choosing at last between his own survival and the passengers' right to be remembered.
about_author: Lena Sterling is a former aviation logistics analyst who spent a decade in border towns across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people erased by systems too large to name.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Ivo Voss, working under his fourth identity in a Baltic port city, takes an unattributable case: a widow insists her husband's flight landed but no airline admits it existed. His POV establishes his paranoid routines and loneliness; the beat is wary curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Two Hundred and Twelve
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews three families who all remember Flight 4471 boarding in Riga. Airline records show the tail number retired years ago. His POV; the emotional beat is the first crack in his belief that paperwork equals truth.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: A retired air traffic controller, drunk and terrified, tells Ivo the plane climbed to an impossible altitude and then 'was never there.' Third-person limited on the controller; dread builds as he begs Ivo to forget he ever spoke.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Ivo discovers the word ERASURE stamped in a leaked procurement file—a data-scrubbing contract spanning three governments. His POV; the beat shifts from investigation to hunted realization that the file names him as a person of interest.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew My Face
chapters.summary: An assassin codenamed Marrow corners Ivo in a tram tunnel—and lets him go, saying 'Not yet.' Marrow's POV reveals he recognizes Ivo from a shared past neither will name. The beat is chilling mercy.

chapters.title: Burn the Apartment
chapters.summary: Ivo's safe flat is torched hours after he leaves; his fourth identity dies in the fire officially. His POV; panic and grief for the small life he'd built, and the decision to run toward the truth instead of away.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Ivo slips into Poland using forged papers bought from a smuggler who asks no questions. Tense cat-and-mouse with border police; his POV carries the theme of survival's price—he abandons the last photo of his real self.

chapters.title: The Fifth Passenger
chapters.summary: A manifest fragment shows 213 boarded, not 212—one name redacted at a level above governments. Ivo's POV; obsession sharpens as he realizes the extra passenger may be the whole point of the erasure.

chapters.title: Marrow's Contract
chapters.summary: Marrow receives orders to terminate Ivo before the summit, but requests a delay, lying that the target is compromised. Marrow's POV exposes his conflict: Ivo once testified to save him from a firing squad.

chapters.title: Archive of Ash
chapters.summary: In a Warsaw basement archive, Ivo meets Nadia Rezek, a disgraced crash investigator keeping her own forbidden copies. Dual POV; the beat is cautious alliance—two people who trust nothing learning to share a flashlight.

chapters.title: What the Cargo Was
chapters.summary: Nadia's files reveal Flight 4471 carried not people alone but a captured defector and encrypted proof of a war crime committed by a future summit signatory. Ivo's POV; moral vertigo—the treaty being celebrated is built on burial.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Ivo maps the conspiracy: each government scrubbed the flight to protect its own piece of the crime. His POV, cold and methodical; the emotional beat is despair at how ordinary the evil looks on spreadsheets.

chapters.title: Safehouse Sermon
chapters.summary: Nadia tells Ivo why she was disgraced: she refused to falsify a crash report years ago. Her POV; vulnerability and resolve, and the first moment either says aloud that they might die for this.

chapters.title: The Widow's Tape
chapters.summary: The Riga widow gives Ivo her husband's last voicemail: 'If we land wrong, tell them we were here.' Ivo's POV; grief becomes fuel, transforming the case into a promise.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Marrow ambushes Ivo at a rail yard but kills only the surveillance team shadowing him, warning: 'They're closer than me.' Marrow's POV; the debt of honor tightens into open betrayal of his employers.

chapters.title: Black Box Rumor
chapters.summary: Nadia confirms the flight recorder survived—it was pulled from a lake by a salvage crew and never logged. Ivo's POV; hope arrives like a heartbeat, immediately shadowed by the question of who holds it now.

chapters.title: The Salvage Captain
chapters.summary: Ivo tracks the salvage captain to a decaying shipyard; the man demands asylum in exchange for the box's location. His POV; the price of survival made literal—another life bartered against the truth.

chapters.title: Summit Countdown
chapters.summary: Fourteen days to the summit. News cycles celebrate the treaty; the vanished flight is a non-event everywhere. Ivo's POV watching the world cheer its own amnesia; the beat is isolation sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: Trap at the Cathedral
chapters.summary: A meet arranged through the captain is a trap; Nadia is taken while Ivo escapes wounded. His POV; guilt detonates—the cost of trusting anyone, including himself.

chapters.title: Marrow's Terms
chapters.summary: Marrow finds the bleeding Ivo and offers a trade: the black box location for Ivo walking away forever. Ivo's POV; the central temptation of the book offered plainly, and refused in a whisper.

chapters.title: What Ivo Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ivo's POV: the testimony years ago that forced him into hiding, and the colleague he abandoned to save himself. The beat is confession; survival's original sin surfaces.

chapters.title: Prisoner of Quiet
chapters.summary: Nadia, held in a black site, resists interrogation by reciting passenger names aloud until her captors flinch. Her POV; defiance as memory-keeping, the theme of inheritance embodied.

chapters.title: The Lake at Night
chapters.summary: Ivo dives the lake with borrowed gear and finds the empty recovery crate—and a tracker left inside. His POV; terror under black water, surfacing to sirens. He runs again, lighter and more desperate.

chapters.title: Double Blind
chapters.summary: Ivo feeds the tracker false coordinates while Marrow covers his escape, openly at war with his handlers now. Alternating POV; uneasy brotherhood forged in gunfire, both men paying interest on old debts.

chapters.title: The Redacted Name
chapters.summary: Decrypted fragments reveal the 213th passenger: the defector's daughter, smuggled aboard as insurance—and alive, hidden by one honest customs officer. Ivo's POV; the mission gains a face and a future.

chapters.title: Finding Ana
chapters.summary: Ivo locates Ana, twelve years old, living under a guardian's silence. Her POV briefly; fear and stubborn courage. Ivo must decide whether involving her protects or spends her.

chapters.title: Guardian's Bargain
chapters.summary: The customs officer agrees to help only if Ivo guarantees Ana reaches the summit press corps personally. His POV; inheritance literalized—a child inheriting her father's truth and his enemies.

chapters.title: Nadia's Silence
chapters.summary: Nadia breaks under a staged execution threat and gives up a false location, buying time. Her POV; shame and cunning braided together—she lied well enough to survive, badly enough to hate it.

chapters.title: Exchange at the Freight Yard
chapters.summary: Ivo trades the salvage captain's freedom for the box's true custodian: a dying archivist inside the summit security apparatus itself. His POV; every ally costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Inside the Perimeter
chapters.summary: Using Marrow's credentials, Ivo infiltrates summit security as a contractor. Tense procedural tension in his POV; invisibility weaponized at last—the skills of hiding turned toward exposure.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Room
chapters.summary: The archivist, oxygen tube in nose, hands over the black box and a full copy of the erasure order, asking only to hear the recording played once. His POV; dignity at the end, memory as legacy.

chapters.title: Voice from 4471
chapters.summary: Ivo plays the cockpit and cabin audio: the final minutes, the passengers' calm, the defector sealing the evidence. His POV shattered open; the dead speak and he cannot look away.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Price
chapters.summary: The archivist's clinic is raided; Marrow extracts Ivo and Ana but is gravely wounded covering them. Marrow's POV; the debt finally paid in blood, forgiveness asked without words.

chapters.title: Three Borders in One Night
chapters.summary: A desperate overland run to the capital with Ana and the dying Marrow, dodging checkpoints. Rotating POV; exhaustion, loyalty, and the recurring choice to keep moving when stopping means safety.

chapters.title: The Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Treaty signing tomorrow; the conspirators move to scrub Ivo's last allies. Nadia, freed in the chaos, reunites with him. Her POV; reunion without relief—they both know what tomorrow requires.

chapters.title: Press Room Gambit
chapters.summary: Ivo gets Ana and the evidence to the international press corps, but the feed is cut mid-broadcast. His POV; hope raised and guillotined, the cruelest beat in the book.

chapters.title: Climax: The Rooftop Frequency
chapters.summary: Ivo hijacks the summit venue's emergency broadcast antenna from the roof while Marrow holds the stairwell and Nadia streams to foreign satellites. All three POVs interleave; the truth goes out raw and unstoppable as Marrow falls.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Flight 4471's 212 names lead every broadcast; two ministers resign, one flees, treaties stall. Ivo's POV amid the noise he caused; vindication tastes like ash because Marrow's body is still warm.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: A public memorial where Ana reads her father's last letter and the crowd answers each name. Nadia's POV; grief transmuted into inheritance—the survivors carry the dead forward.

chapters.title: The First Name Again
chapters.summary: Ivo retires his four aliases and reclaims his birth name publicly at the inquiry, accepting arrest, testimony, and whatever follows. Final POV; the price of survival paid in reverse—he buys back himself with the truth.
